REASON FOR REFERRALU: 

Confirmation of SNRPB variant detected in the 100,000 Genomes Project
Patient and sibling has been diagnosed with skeletal dysplasia*. However, patient's sister and father are both clinically unaffected (information supplied with referral). Patient and his relatives were tested as part of the pilot of the Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project using a virtual panel of genes associated with skeletal dysplasia**. The heterozygous variant of uncertain clinical significance, SNRPB c.607A>G p.(Met203Val) was detected by Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS). Confirmation of this variant in an accredited diagnostic laboratory has been requested.
UTEST

Test for the SNRPB variant by bidirectional fluorescent Sanger DNA Sequencing.

URESULTS

Michael LOWETH: 
Heterozygous SNRPB c.607A>G p.(Met203Val) variant detected

John LOWETH: 
Heterozygous SNRPB c.607A>G p.(Met203Val) variant detected

Victoria HOUGHTON: 
Variant NOT detected

Peter LOWETH: 
Variant NOT detected

U

SUMMARYU 

The presence of the SNRPB c.607A>G p.(Met203Val) variant is confirmed in Michael and John LOWETH.

This variant was NOT detected in Victoria HOUGHTON or Peter LOWETH. 
The clinical significance of this variant remains uncertain1. Missense variants in this gene have been reported to cause cerebrocostomandibular syndrome2, however, these are located in another region of this gene and are predicted to affect alternative splicing.

FURTHER WORK

If appropriate, Michael?s mother could be tested to investigate the possible significance of this variant. Referral to Clinical Genetics for genetic counselling is recommended prior to testing.

If appropriate, other affected members of this family could be tested to investigate the possible significance of this variant. Referral to Clinical Genetics for genetic counselling is recommended prior to testing.
nUNotes

*HPO terms submitted for this individual included: skeletal dysplasia, Genu Valgum and short stature.
** The Unexplained skeletal dysplasia v1.3 gene panel was used by the 100,000 Genomes project for analysis

SNRPB gene nomenclature based on GenBank accession number NG_042057.1 where nucleotide number 1 corresponds to the first base of the translation initiation codon.

1Assessment of pathogenicity carried out using bioinformatics software Opal by Fabric Genomics designed specifically for the 100,000 Genomes project. 

2 OMIM reference *182282, http://www.omim.org.
